decision: set the finish line: from the video alone, read names, hole cards with owners, board, button and blinds, and every action with amount; all must match the hand-read YAML, each action time within 3 s of it, in under 1.0 s per hand (median of 5 warm runs) and under $0.10
why: the user asked for under 1 s and under $0.10 per game and to keep frame-by-frame reading only as the check
evidence: examples/real/wpt_rolling_thunder.yaml

decision: measured the floor: decoding every frame of the 7.5 min clip takes 6.6 s on 16 cores; listing packets takes 0.14 s; 97 keyframes, one every 4.6 s on average (max 5.3 s); GPU decode (d3d11va) fails to start
why: decoding is the cost every approach pays, so it had to be known before choosing one
evidence: %TEMP%/pm-fast/probe_decode.py and probe_keys.py output in session d997c2e1
result: decoding everything can never fit in 1 s; decode keyframes, then only gaps that changed

decision: read the TV graphics instead of the felt: they show the acting player, both hole cards, name, TO CALL amount, pot, blinds, ante and board
why: the graphics are clean fixed pictures, so reading them is cheaper and surer than spotting real cards on the table
evidence: session files real-frames/ev_01.jpg, ev_04.jpg, ev_15.jpg

decision: work out seats, button and blinds from who acts in what order and their TO CALL amounts, not from a separate model
why: the graphics never show the button, but Ian TO CALL 30,000 with blinds 30K/60K marks him small blind, and preflop order fixes the other seats
evidence: session files real-frames/ev_04.jpg

decision: risk found: Ping is on screen only 13.0 to 15.5 s, between keyframes at 10.7 and 16.0, so keyframes alone miss him and his cards
why: short turns hide between keyframes; the gaps where the acting player changes must be decoded too
evidence: probe_keys.py keyframe list; YAML events s3 fold 00:13, s4 fold 00:15.5

decision: rigor medium: private branch and easy to undo, but every speed and accuracy number comes from a script, run more than once
why: the numbers are the deliverable here, so they need repeatable checks; the blast radius is small
evidence: branch poker-memory-mvp

decision: planned 9 units, riskiest first: keyframe decoding, reading the graphics, existing-card-model bakeoff, turning graphics into a hand, timing inside gaps, speed, CLI and tests, report
why: each unit ends in a check on the real clip, so a wrong turn shows up before the next unit builds on it
evidence: session todos fr-harness .. fr-report

decision: skipped a design bakeoff for the code shape; the reader returns the same hand record the YAML already uses
why: a new optional module is easy to undo, and reusing the record lets the existing engine validate the reader output for free
evidence: src/poker_memory/model.py:146 HandRecord

decision: unit frames: decode keyframes in-process with PyAV (auto threads) and decode a gap only where something changed
why: keyframes take 0.155 s for all 97; one gap costs 0.083 s; 16 gaps in parallel threads cost 0.641 s because the decoder already uses every core; every frame costs 6.26 s
evidence: scripts/bench_decode.py, median of 5 runs, PyAV 19.0.2, 16 cores
result: kept: keyframes fit the budget; gaps must stay under about 6

decision: no pretrained card model in the reader; read card slots directly: suit from colour, rank by OCR
why: research found no card model trained on TV graphics or four-colour decks, and Ultralytics-trained weights are AGPL; overlay cards sit at fixed spots so detection is not needed
evidence: session file fast-reader-research.md Q1, Q5

decision: vision-language models only as the verifier, never in the fast path
why: they cost 0.003 to 0.03 dollars per hand but take seconds before the first answer, so they cannot meet 1 s
evidence: fast-reader-research.md Q6 latency table

decision: RapidOCR recognition-only on fixed crops, cached by pixel signature
why: probe read every test crop right (names, TO CALL 60,000, pot, ranks, board A57J) but costs about 8 ms per crop even batched, because each crop is padded to 320 px wide; so read each distinct crop once
evidence: pm-fast ocr_probe.py and ocr_batch.py on keyframes 10.7, 106.8, 138.8
result: kept; per-crop cost is the next thing to cut

decision: decode the gaps between keyframes in parallel, one core per decoder
why: PyAV lets go of the Python lock while decoding, so many small single-core decoders beat a few multi-core ones on short gaps
evidence: scripts/bench_decode.py median of 5: 16 gaps 0.625 s with every decoder on all cores, 0.437 s with 1 core each (4,068 frames/s overall), 0.427 s with 2 cores each 8 at a time
result: kept; 1 core each is simplest and as fast

decision: no decoder shortcut exists; only decoding fewer frames saves time
why: the VP9 decoder ignores skip_loop_filter and skip_frame=NONREF
evidence: probe_skip.py: output byte-identical either way, about 123 ms per 128-frame gap on one core
result: decode only gaps whose two ends look different, and stop each gap early

decision: panel found by a dark strip left of card 1 plus two bright card slots, tried at 4 slots x 2 slide offsets
why: six brightness averages per picture, no model
evidence: probe_panel.py on 10 frames: right offset reads cards 120-170 and strip 43-56; wrong offsets read strip >= 104 or card <= 71
result: misses a panel while its cards are still flying in; treated as no panel

decision: rank by OCR at width 96, only on settled crops, reading a lone 0/O/D as Q
why: fast and exact once the card stops moving
evidence: probe_rank.py: 52/52 right at 2.9 ms each on settled frames; width 48 made mistakes; a mid-fade frame read Q as 0
result: a crop must be seen in two pictures before it is read

decision: suit from the colour of the card ink (4-colour deck), not OCR
why: colour separates the four suits with wide margins and costs a few averages
evidence: probe_suit.py on 52 cards: hearts Cr +37..45, diamonds Cb +36..45, clubs Cb and Cr -19..-29, spades about 0
result: rule: Cr > 20 hearts, Cb > 20 diamonds, both < -10 clubs, else spades

decision: graphics rules: a preflop fold is the panel being replaced (no FOLD text); statuses clear when a betting round ends; an event is timed from the first picture that differs from the settled one before it
why: the overlay lags the table by 1-3 s, so timing from the start of each change keeps the error smallest
evidence: gap sheets early.png and late.png: David replaced by Ping at 14 s; the raise types in over 40-48 s; Ian's fold fades from about 426.5 s
result: the 07:04 fold may land about 3 s after the hand-read time; watch it

decision: stacks are never on screen: an all-in gives that stack exactly; every other seat gets the least stack that fits what it put in plus its last TO CALL, said so in the seat note
why: the finish line leaves stacks out; making stack optional would ripple through engine, memory and 76 tests
evidence: engine.py:82 needs a stack per seat; memory.py:257 uses the hero stack for pot odds, so it must cover the TO CALL
result: pot odds at the big decision stay right; other stacks are lower bounds and the report says so

decision: first full run fixed: dim status cut, face-up test, trimmed name crops, UNREAD runs skipped in action timing
why: run 1 crashed: Ping missing, JOE/JOET split, card backs read as Ks, all-in read late, fades broke timing
evidence: %TEMP%/pm-fast/run1.py after fixes: record validates, cards/owners/board/button/stakes match the YAML, 15 of 16 events within 3 s
result: record correct; s1 fold 3.1 s late (graphics lag), 5.05 s warm

decision: threads stay; a process pool is rejected
why: gap decode is 7.29 s on 1 thread, 1.27 s on 16 threads; with look() and early stop 2.77 s because numpy and decode fight over the GIL
evidence: procs.py: spawning 16 processes ~3 s; warm 16/12/8 procs 1.38/1.69/1.56 s, no better than threads
result: kept ThreadPoolExecutor; cut work per gap instead

decision: replace timestamp seeks with one demux pass and a fresh decoder per gap fed from the keyframe packet
why: 9 of 97 seeks land one keyframe early (10.68 21.36 96.10 101.44 128.13 234.91 256.26 261.60 309.65), about 1035 wasted frames, ~395 in scanned gaps; each open+seek costs 5-7 ms
evidence: demux of all 10730 packets 0.096 s; decode floor 1.52 ms/frame on one core (1.35 ms with 2 slice threads)

decision: presence test must not lean on the dark gap strip
why: a bright fur hat behind the see-through panels lifts the gap mean to 80-81 and hides Ian's panel at 357.70 364.54 376.26 416.42 427.10 (8 flicker gaps, ~227 frames); a false slot-2 panel at 250.92 adds ~126 frames
evidence: probe: present panels show card insets 151-169 with >30% pixels over 200 (face) or ~154 flat (back); gap 47-81

decision: no constant lag fudge on event times
why: graphics lag the table by 0-3 s and it varies per event; a fudge fitted to this one hand would hide the real error
evidence: offsets -0.6..+3.1 s across 16 events
result: times reported as read; the 3.1 s fold is called out

decision: panel presence: both card spots hold a card (white face: over 25% of pixels above 200; grey back: 2-px inset mean 140-170, std dev under 20) and the name bar is dark (median under 110)
why: the dark-gap-strip test failed when a bright hat sat behind the see-through panels
evidence: check_fast_read: all 5 seats' names and hole cards right
result: done in look_all; replaces the pending row above

decision: workers only decode; one thread reads every picture, in batches
why: numpy lets go of the interpreter lock in every call and must win it back; reading on many threads thrashes the lock
evidence: earlier: decode+look on all threads 2.77 s; now between = 0.70 s

decision: _percentiles: one np.partition over the whole stack, reproducing np.percentile's linear interpolation exactly
why: np.percentile per crop was many small calls
evidence: batched look_all identical to per-picture look on 542 pictures
result: unit test against np.percentile still owed

decision: ffmpeg decoder skip options stay off
why: none made the native vp9 decoder faster on this clip
evidence: probe in an earlier segment: no measurable change

decision: stop rule kept: a gap stops at the first picture matching the next keyframe; an empty screen never ends a gap
why: before the flop each panel shows only briefly, with empty screens between
evidence: tighter stop rules lost states; check stays 26/27

decision: OCR runtime knobs left at defaults
why: the model run itself was 310 of 320 ms
evidence: threads 1/2/4/8/16 = 1465/791/447/306/355 ms; 5 calls at once best 370 ms; one big call no better
result: shrink the model instead (see model row)

decision: clip times in integer maths: pts * numerator / denominator
why: Fraction maths per packet was slow
evidence: same floats as float(pts * time_base)

decision: look_all reads every waiting picture in one numpy pass
why: fewer numpy calls means fewer lock hand-offs
evidence: identical looks on 542 pictures; warm run to ~1.50 s

decision: keep threads and 16 workers; no process pool
why: this 8-core/16-thread VM is the limit, not the interpreter lock
evidence: 31 gaps/2593 frames: processes 0.589-0.633 s vs threads 0.619-0.633 s; workers 8/12/14/16/20 = 1.47/1.36/1.33/1.38/1.40 s (noise); 16 jobs at once run ~2.2x slower each
result: total work ~6.6 core-s on ~6.5 cores of throughput: ~1.0 s floor, so cut work

decision: Catalog in exact integers with a growing mask stack
why: float band maths and per-add allocation were slow
evidence: twin check: 0 differences over 4800 adds, 477 same_look, 523 strip distances

decision: swap RapidOCR's default Chinese PP-OCRv4 recogniser for PaddleOCR's en_number_mobile_v2.0 (1.9 MB, Apache-2.0), shipped in the package
why: OCR was 1.47 of ~6.6 core-s
evidence: 82 real crops: 351 -> 73 ms (8 threads), 1491 -> 154 ms (1 thread); en_PP-OCRv3 only 277 ms and lost the stakes read; 2 crop meanings changed (a partial TO CALL loses its amount; a mid-slide hole card reads T at 0.41) and both are outvoted
result: check 26/27 unchanged; warm 1.40 -> 1.17 s, cold 2.84 -> 1.70 s

decision: no OCR confidence cutoff
why: right reads score 0.49 and 0.51, the wrong one 0.41: a cutoff would be fitted to this clip
evidence: ocrscores.py on the 82 crops
result: per-seat majority vote over time handles one-off misreads

decision: Catalog: skip the band maths when the total of differing pixels is already under the limit; search all numbers on bit-packed columns
why: match was 0.151 s, status search 42.5 ms of it
evidence: fast path covers 3766 of 4511 hint matches; only 44 masks were identical, so a same-mask shortcut was dropped; twin check 0 differences over 4800 adds

decision: scan reads the file and looks at every keyframe before any stretch starts (hybrid design C), not a streaming scan
why: streaming left the reader behind: batches swelled to 64 pictures, stop checks came late, more frames were decoded past the stop point
evidence: ab.py 4 rounds x 3 warm: old 1.245 s, streaming 1.278 s, hybrid 1.182 s warm median; cold 1.880 / 1.806 / 1.726 s; output identical

decision: each stretch decodes at most LEASH=3 pictures before the reader judges them (design J, one shared pool)
why: 16 to 18% of decoded frames (about 500) came after the stop point
evidence: probe_over.py: 3,060 frames decoded where 2,562 were needed; with the leash 3,180 -> 2,670 decoded; throttle.py leash 1/2/3/4: 0.661/0.652/0.644/0.661 s for the stretches; identical output

decision: cut the reader's cost per picture: counts, uint16 totals, squares only for candidate slots, radix percentiles, uint32 suit sums
why: in phase 2 the one reader thread was the bottleneck
evidence: look_all alone 0.66 -> 0.30 ms per picture; ref.py IDENTICAL

decision: read the whole file before decoding keyframes (read-first Clip.read)
why: reading while workers decode makes every packet wait for the interpreter lock
evidence: ab.py 4 x 3 warm at 17-20% load: 1.065 vs 1.119 s, scan 0.884 vs 0.939 s; IDENTICAL

decision: pool size stays os.cpu_count() after the leash and read-first
why: the VM's cores are the limit, not the pool
evidence: 16, 14 and 12 workers within noise, 10 slower; 24/32/48 workers 7 to 13 ms slower

decision: stop cutting the reader
why: phase 2 is bound by decoding about 2,700 VP9 pictures, not by reading the graphics
evidence: probe_freereader.py paired: scan 0.938 s with the real reader vs 0.885 s with a near-free cached one (at most 57 ms to gain); decode-only floor 0.711 s median for the same 2,712 frames

decision: no fewer-workers-with-tile-threads mix
why: splitting one picture over threads costs more CPU in total, and every core is already busy
evidence: probe_ab_mix.py 15 paired rounds against 16 x 1 (1.026 s): 8x2 129 ms slower, 10x2 96, 12x2 77, 6x3 187; tile threads on every decoder 100-133 ms slower

decision: phase 3: number one kind at a time (status, name, hole, board) and OCR each kind on a worker once numbered; stakes OCR after the numbering
why: OCR beside numbering slows the numbering about 1:1 (interpreter lock, ORT spinning), so only the big status OCR overlapping the rest pays
evidence: probe_p3.py 30 paired rounds: C 18.1 ms faster (28/30), all-OCR-in-background no gain; in read_hand vs vW, 20 rounds: phase 3 172.9 -> 152.4 ms, faster 20/20; IDENTICAL; check 26/27
result: kept; Ocr call counter now behind a lock

decision: uint8 same() and an exact shortcut in Catalog.add: a mask byte-equal to the last mask given its hint gets that number
why: build spends about 19.5 of its 25 ms in same() on board strips; most hint matches are exact repeats
evidence: probe_same.py on real pairs, every variant exact: strips 6.0 -> about 5 us per call; after add(m) returns h, same(masks[h], m) holds, so the shortcut cannot change a result; ref.py IDENTICAL

decision: stretches start in time order
why: no cheap size guess picks out the long stretches: packet bytes correlate only 0.55 with decode time
evidence: probe_order.py simulation at 65% load: time order 720 ms, most bytes first 765 ms, perfect longest-first 653 ms (67 ms at best)

decision: the last 6 stretches to start decode with 4 slice threads (LATE=6, TAIL_THREADS=4)
why: the last stretches start at 530-630 ms and run 230-290 ms each on one core while other cores finish; a 1280-wide VP9 picture has 4 tile columns
evidence: probe_tiles2.py: one stretch 1.85 ms/frame on 1 thread, 0.89 on 4; probe_ab_multi.py 15 rounds: 6x4 18.6 ms faster (12/15), 10x4 24.7 (10/15), 4x4 23.2 (8/15), 10x2 and 15x2 slower; vs vY 20 rounds 13.4 ms faster (17/20); slice threads give bit-identical frames, IDENTICAL

decision: no skipping VP9 frames inside a stretch, no frame threads
why: each inter frame uses the previous frame's motion vectors and probability contexts; frame threads hand pictures back late, which breaks the leash
evidence: VP9 decoding rules; stretch() assumes one picture per packet

decision: numbering stays after the scan, not in its idle tail
why: numbering must follow time order and holds the interpreter lock, which would delay the tail decoders on the critical path
evidence: probe_tail3.py: every keyframe done by 180 ms, the last stretches end the scan

decision: load the OCR model on a worker during the scan instead of before it
why: a fresh process spent 0.5 s importing rapidocr and loading the model before decoding began
evidence: cold_ab.py, 8 paired fresh processes at 16-29% load: wall 2.69 -> 2.39 s (310 ms faster, 8/8), same hand in all 18; the scan slows about 220 ms but the model is always ready (wait 0 ms); warm probe_ab_inproc 12 rounds: 5.7 ms slower, 5/12 (noise)

decision: stop the speed loop: warm reads are under 1 s; a fresh process is not and cannot be here
why: what is left is decoding about 2,700 VP9 pictures on 8 physical cores; Python, numpy and av imports alone take about 0.35 s and the scan about 0.8 s, so a fresh process cannot finish in 1 s
evidence: bench_fast_read.py at 8-22% load: warm 0.965 s median of 7 (0.958-0.976), 10.4 of 16 cores busy, scan 0.813 s; fresh process 2.194 s median of 5 (2.170-2.306), imports 0.823 s; same hand in all 13 reads; vA vs now in one process, 10 alternating rounds: 1.038 -> 0.936 s, faster 10/10; check_fast_read 26/27
result: warm about 0.94-0.97 s per hand; keep the reader running (server, or one command reading many videos) to stay under 1 s

decision: add the command poker-memory read VIDEO...: prints the stakes and the hand as session-file YAML, and reads every video given in one process
why: a command is how people will use the reader, and one process reading many videos is how a read stays under 1 s
evidence: read of the clip given twice: 1.18 s then 0.96 s, the same hand both times; tests/test_reader.py adds 23 tests (parsers, the exact shortcuts against plain versions, build on a made-up hand, the read command against the hand read by eye); 3 deliberate breaks were each caught; full pytest 99 passed

decision: measured again on commit 53a3a30 before reporting; README now says 0.97 to 1.0 s warm and gives the spread
why: the finish line is a warm median under 1.0 s and this VM is shared, so one run is not enough; overlapping the numbering with the scan stays parked (entry 51)
evidence: bench_fast_read.py --cold 5 --runs 7 at 8 to 9 pct host load: warm median 0.995 s, range 0.965 to 1.023 s, 10.0 of 16 cores busy; fresh 2.235 s (imports 0.839 s); every read gave the same hand. Earlier run 0.965 s (0.958 to 0.976)
result: met at the median in both runs, with 5 to 35 ms to spare; single reads can cross 1 s on a busy host
